utterance:
That's really helpful — pain starting around the belly button and moving to the right lower side is a pattern I take seriously. A few more questions:
1. Have you felt sick or vomited? How many times?
2. Do you have any appetite at all — would you want to eat?
3. When did you last open your bowels, and was it normal, loose, or hard? Any blood?

reply: Felt sick since the early hours and I threw up once this morning. I could not face breakfast, not hungry at all, which isn't like me. No diarrhoea, I went normally yesterday morning, nothing since, and no blood. Weeing is normal. I felt hot and a bit shivery last night.

utterance: Samuel, I've finished examining you, and I want to be straight with you about what I found. Your pain started around the belly button and moved to the right lower tummy, you've felt sick and vomited, you've lost your appetite, you've had a temperature, and when I examined your tummy there is marked tenderness in the right lower side with pain when I press and release, when you cough, and when I pressed the left side. Put together, this is a classic picture of appendicitis — inflammation of the appendix — and I can't rule out that it's becoming more serious. This needs urgent assessment and likely surgery at the hospital emergency department today, so I'm arranging that transfer now.
reply: Right now? Oh, right. Do I really need to go straight away?

utterance: Yes, I do, and here's why: the appendix can perforate — burst — and that can happen within hours to a day or two of symptoms starting. You've had pain for about fourteen hours already, you have a fever and a fast heart rate, and the examination shows irritation of the lining of your abdomen. Waiting at home risks it bursting, which turns this into a much more serious infection. The good news is that appendicitis is very treatable — the hospital will do a scan, give you fluids and antibiotics, and remove the appendix if needed. I'm not able to safely manage this in the clinic.
reply: Okay then, let us get it done.

awards.label: Phone the emergency department with a handover
Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment

utterance:
Samuel, here's your plan, and please listen carefully:

1. Go to the emergency department now — today, this afternoon. Do not drive yourself; get your mum, a mate, or a taxi. If you can't get a lift within the next hour, call 000 and ask for an ambulance.
2. Do not eat or drink anything from now on — not even water. If the surgeons need to operate, an empty stomach is much safer.
3. You can take the paracetamol I've prescribed — two tablets — if the pain is bad on the way, but please avoid ibuprofen or Nurofen-type anti-inflammatories, as they can irritate the stomach and affect surgery.
4. I've already phoned the emergency department and handed over your details, and I've sent through your blood and urine test requests.
5. Call 000 immediately, or get your driver to go straight to the hospital, if the pain suddenly gets much worse all over your tummy, you feel faint or dizzy, you keep vomiting, or you get shaking chills with a high fever — those would be signs the appendix may be perforating.

You were right to come in, and I'm glad you did — this is exactly the kind of thing that needs to be seen urgently. Is there someone who can drive you right now?
reply: Yeah, my mate is waiting outside in the car for me.
